clips.0_intro: Sahara Relief helps a woman who cannot read claim her quarterly relief payment, in her own language, with a voice to guide her, and with a helper beside her if she needs one. Staff only review the cases the computer is not sure about. Everything you will see is a prototype, with invented people, invented ID numbers and a pretend payment.
clips.1_login: Let's start as the citizen. The login page has one tap demo accounts, to keep the demo quick. A real person would type her email and a six digit PIN on this big number pad. We tap Zainab, a widow who cannot read well.
clips.1_lang: The app opens in Urdu, because that is her language, and every screen has a recorded Urdu voice. For this video, I will switch to English.
clips.1_start: This is her claim page. She taps, Yes, start.
clips.1_tour: Before each page, a short practice demo plays. A hand taps a practice card with made up details, and a voice explains what to do. Nothing in the demo is sent, and it never fills her real boxes. When it ends, she does it herself.
clips.1_consent: First, her permission. The office sees her name, ID number and household. Her helper sees her details only while helping. She can take her permission back at any time, and staff access stops at once.
clips.1_cnic: Now her ID number. She types it on the big number pad, and the system finds her record in the government database and asks: is this you?
clips.1_cnic2: It shows her own record, with the ID number partly hidden. If someone typed another person's number, the system would show only a name, and the papers would be checked against that person's record.
clips.1_house: Next, her household size. The system never shows her the number. She types it, and the system answers only yes or no. Three wrong tries send the claim to a person.
clips.1_front: Now the two photos of her ID card, front first. She taps, Choose a photo.
clips.1_front2: The system reads the name and number off the card, compares the face with the photo in the government record, checks that this really is the front, and checks the photo for blur and editing.
clips.1_back: Then the back of the card. The system also checks that the right side was sent.
clips.1_acct: Her mobile account number: eleven digits, starting with zero three. The system only checks its shape. It never shows anything back, so a stranger cannot learn whose account it is.
clips.1_send: She looks over the summary, and sends her claim.
clips.1_result: Every check passed, and the model is more than ninety seven percent sure, so the system approves the claim by itself. The payment is sent to her account, and staff will call her to confirm.
clips.1_dash: Back on her claim page, one green box tells her the money has been sent. If staff were still checking, it would say so. If staff needed another paper, it would ask for it right here.
clips.2_reset: Now the helper. First I reset the demo, so Zainab has no claim.
clips.2_login: Many women have only a basic phone, so a community helper can claim with her, from his own phone. We log in as Yousuf.
clips.2_families: He sees only the families assigned to him. Her name and ID number are hidden until she gives permission.
clips.2_proof: To open her family, he asks her three things and types the answers: her ID number, her date of birth, and her household size. First, a wrong ID number. The server answers only: these details do not match. It never says which detail was wrong, and three wrong tries lock the family.
clips.2_proof2: Now the right details. The server checks them against the government record and says only yes, so the helper never sees the record. Her permission is recorded as hers, with a line in the diary.
clips.2_claim: He is now helping Zainab. Her ID number and household size were already checked, so the claim goes straight to the ID card photos. He uploads the front and the back.
clips.2_acct: He types her account number, not his own. If a payout account matched any helper's own number, the system would hold the claim for a person.
clips.2_result: Approved. A helper can never approve or reject anything, and he cannot see families that are not his.
clips.2_limit: One honest limit. Software cannot stop a helper asking for cash after the money has arrived. A phone call that asks the woman if she received the full amount is planned, but not built yet.
clips.3_reset: Now the admin. First, another reset, and then a faulty claim from the citizen.
clips.3_faulty: Zainab sends a claim, but this time the name on the card photo does not match the government record.
clips.3_held: The system does not reject her, and it does not approve her. It says: a person will look, and it gives the exact reason.
clips.3_adminlogin: Now we log in as the admin.
clips.3_queue: The review queue lists only claims the computer could not decide, least sure first, and only for the admin's own office, with active consent.
clips.3_case: Here is the case. The decision card shows the zone, the confidence, and every check in plain words. Card versus record has failed: the name on the card does not match the record.
clips.3_notes: The, I am not sure, notes say what was checked, why it is unsure, and what to ask.
clips.3_table: This table puts her registration record, the government record, and what her ID card photo says, side by side. The differences are red.
clips.3_view: The admin can open the paper she sent. Every opening is written to the diary.
clips.3_ask: The admin chooses, Ask for more proof, picks the ID card front, and the system sends her a message.
clips.3_cit: Back on Zainab's claim page, a yellow box shows the request, in her language, with a voice. One tap opens the upload for exactly that paper.
clips.3_resend: She sends a correct front. It is sent by itself, and the system checks it again.
clips.3_fixed: This time everything matches, so the system approves it, and her page shows that the money has been sent.
clips.3_admin2: Back with the admin. Rules are versions, and are never edited in place.
clips.3_twin: The Digital Twin replays past cases under a draft rule, so the admin sees who would change before it goes live.
clips.3_policy: The cost slider shows the price of a wrong approval against a slow one, and where the approval line should sit.
clips.3_eval: The evaluation page shows accuracy, and the false alarms, honestly.
clips.3_diary: And the diary. Verify checks that nobody has changed history.
clips.9_outro: That is Sahara Relief. Two models trained by us, three open source tools, hard rules before any score, a person for every doubtful case, and a diary nobody can edit. It is a prototype on invented data, and we have said where it is limited. Thank you.
